ticket.title: Add miter deps tier 1: crate import edges, --why proof of use and --unused dead dependencies
ticket.description: Tier 1 of the miter deps capability that GB-160 depends on, and the only tier needed for the audit to run. It is a read-only join of two graphs: cargo metadata --format-version 1 says what is declared and resolved, the AST says what is actually used, and nothing in the Rust ecosystem joins them (cargo-udeps is nightly and crate-granular, cargo tree is path-only). Scope: (1) default table of consumer crate to provider crate edges with distinct symbol counts and files touched; (2) --why <dep>, the shortest declared path plus proof of use, naming the symbols the consumer actually references, so the answer is reason and not just route; (3) --unused, declared dependencies with zero referenced symbols split by normal/dev/build, which is how a dead dependency such as the unused miter-ast in dado-core gets caught by a gate instead of by accident; (4) --format table|json with a stable schema and meaningful exit codes so it can gate CI. Reuse analysis::references and inventory crate discovery; do not reimplement resolution. Feature analysis is deliberately out of scope (GB-163).
acceptance_criteria: miter deps --format json reports crate edges for all eleven repositories
miter deps --why miter-storage from rabbet names the path via chalkline-core and miter-engine plus the symbols rabbet itself uses
miter deps --unused finds a dependency with no referenced symbols in a fixture crate and exits non-zero

verification_receipt.summary: miter deps tier 1: crate edges + --why + --unused; 160 engine tests green, clippy and fmt clean; dogfood at the meta-harness root finds 42 crates, 132 edges, 59 declared-but-unused; storypole reports 3 dead deps verified by grep; module-shadow false positive fixed (pub use outfeed::* is a local module)

task.title: Add miter deps: per-crate import edges, symbol counts and feature-gated items
task.description: P0 of GB-160. miter answers symbol-level questions (references, impact) but cannot aggregate crate-to-crate import edges with symbol counts, nor see which items sit behind #[cfg(feature)] - the two raw inputs to a crate-vs-feature decision. Add a deps subcommand: for each workspace member, the provider crates it imports from with distinct symbol counts, the items that are feature-gated, and JSON output. Model it on the clones subcommand. This must land before the suite audit so the audit is measurement rather than anecdote.
